items.title: Pelinka: Lakers Will Be Active Before Trade Deadline
items.summary: The Lakers underwent a roster upheaval during the offseason and they’re not through making changes. General manager Rob Pelinka declared on Friday he will be “active” over the next few months to make more upgrades, he said on a Spectrum Sportsnet interview (video link, hat tip to Real GM). “We’ll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see,” Pelinka said. “We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. items.summary: James Harden’s slow start to 2026/27 has led to some consternation in Cleveland, but the Cavaliers guard erupted for a season-high 51 points in Friday’s NBA Cup victory over Indiana, according to ESPN. Harden, who passed Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history with 26, is the fourth-oldest player to score 50-plus points in a game. The 37-year-old, who was plus-22 in 40 minutes, shot 15-of-26 from the field, including 7-of-11 from three-point range. He also made all 14 of his free throws in addition to having six rebounds and six assists. “That was vintage,” Cavs head coach Kenny Atkinson said. “You really can’t do anything if you’re the opposing coach. There’s nothing you can do, especially when he’s getting by you like that. You know, when they started taking away the step-back and he, you know, one or two crosses and he’s in the lane, then there’s just no stopping…

items.summary: Veteran center Jusuf Nurkic will be sidelined at least one more week due to the toe injury on his right foot, the Jazz announced in a press release. According to the team, Nurkic is making progress in his recovery and has been participating in on-court work. The 32-year-old big man will be reevaluated again in seven days. Nurkic suffered a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe in his right foot during Utah’s preseason opener on October 4. He has been sidelined for the past six-plus weeks and will miss at least one more. Nurkic was limited to 41 appearances in 2025/26, his first season in Utah, but he made 36 starts and averaged 10.9 points, 10.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists in 26.4 minutes per night while shooting 50.3% from the field.
